scenario: Diabetes review in a woman with tingling feet; HbA1c and statin added.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Hello Meena, come in. Sorry to keep you waiting, we are running late today.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: It is fine, doctor. I was just checking the cricket score on my phone. India are doing very well today.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: I saw that. So, this is your sugar review, correct?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Yes doctor. I have come for my diabetes check, and also my feet have been tingling at night.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: How long has the tingling been going on?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Maybe two months, maybe three. I am not very sure.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: And how long have you had diabetes?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: I have had sugar for eight years now.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Which tablets are you taking for it?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Glycomet, five hundred milligrams, twice a day after food. Um, I think I miss the night one maybe twice a week.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Okay. Any blurring of vision, or passing urine very often?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: No blurring of vision. But yes, I get up two times at night to pass urine.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Anyone in the family with sugar or heart problems?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: My mother had sugar also, and my father had a heart attack at sixty.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Any allergy to any medicine?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Um, I think I was allergic to something once, some antibiotic, but I do not remember the name.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Alright. Let me check your pressure. It is a hundred and thirty over eighty. Your pulse is 78.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Is that high, doctor?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: A little above where we want it. Now let me see your feet. The pulses are fine, but the sensation is reduced on the left foot. This could be early nerve damage from the sugar, but we will see the reports.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doctor, will I need insulin one day? My neighbour was put on injections and I am scared.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Not at this stage. I want to repeat your HbA1c and a fasting sugar today, and a kidney test also.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Okay. Same tablets then?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Continue the glycomet, and take it regularly with food, both times. I will add atorvastatin 10 milligrams at night because of your family history of heart disease.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Okay. When should I come again?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Come back in three months with the reports, and I will review your sugar then. Check your feet every day for cuts.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Thank you doctor.

gold.key: get up two times at night to pass urine
a hundred and thirty over eighty
sensation is reduced on the left foot

notes: Cricket and the waiting time in turns 0 to 2 are small talk and unlabelled. Turn 5 duration is hedged (maybe two months, maybe three). Turn 9 contains an unlabelled adherence remark (misses the night dose maybe twice a week). Turn 15 is a deliberately vague allergy statement (some antibiotic, name forgotten) labelled uncertain. Turn 17 (is that high) is a plain question, not labelled as a concern. Doctor continues glycomet (same as patient takes) and adds atorvastatin (new). HbA1c may be pronounced letter by letter by a speech synthesiser.
